title: Risk Analysis — Market, Technical, and Depreciation Risks
description: Identify and quantify risks associated with each recommendation. Cover: (1) Used/Refurb Market Risk: RTX 3090 used market — mining card risk, wear level, warranty status, how to verify condition, return policies. (2) New Product Depreciation Risk: RTX 50-series just launched — will prices drop? will 60-series make 50-series obsolete? timing analysis for purchase decision. (3) Compatibility Risk: driver issues (Linux vs Windows), framework support (does llama.cpp support this GPU?), motherboard PCIe slot version (PCIe 3.0 vs 4.0 bandwidth impact), power connector availability. (4) Supply Chain Risk: availability, lead times, regional pricing differences (US vs China vs EU), import duties. (5) Performance Degradation Risk: will the GPU maintain performance over time? thermal degradation? (6) Cloud Alternative Risk: if cloud becomes cheaper, when does the math flip? (7) Model Evolution Risk: if 70B models become the norm, will 24GB VRAM be insufficient? (8) eGPU Specific Risks: PCIe bandwidth loss (typically 20-30%), enclosure cost ($300-500), Thunderbolt compatibility, thermal throttling in enclosures. Each risk must include: likelihood (high/medium/low), impact (high/medium/low), mitigation strategy, and monitoring indicator (how to know if the risk materializes).
outputs: risk register with likelihood/impact/mitigation for each risk
